newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei ends just below 21,000 on US election.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei ends just below 21,000 on US election.

text.p: Japan's key stock index surged to end just below 21,000 on Wednesday, relieved by Bill Clinton's re-election as U.S. president and the Republicans' retention of control in Congress. The market's next focus will be the announcement of Japan's new cabinet members, brokers said.
The Nikkei 225 average soared 399.19 points, or 1.94 percent, to finish at 20,991.52. Its December futures were 480 points higher at 21,100.
"The Republicans' keeping control of the House eased fears of possible dollar falls and pushed up the stocks," said Shigenori Okazaki, a political analyst at S.B.C. Warburg.
The TOPIX index ended up 19.37 points, or 1.25 percent, at 1,573.17.
The Nikkei 300 average jumped 3.79 points or 1.30 percent to 295.05.
Gainers beat losers 934 to 173, while 131 issues were unchanged.
"There was some somewhat speculative arbitrage trade involving buying of stocks and selling of bonds," said Hiroshi Morimoto, general manager at Daiwa Securities.
Such movements were prompted by the recent overheating of the Japanese government bond market, brokers said.

Analysts said the market would be mainly watching to see whether Hashimoto, forced to form a minority government after failing to put together a new coalition, would assemble a team to carry out political and economic reforms.
In sectors, advancers were led by fisheries, real estate, warehousing, gas and railway/bus. There were no major retreating sectors.
The yen's easing against the dollar helped to lift export-related shares, such as those of car firms.
Shares of Honda Motor Co Ltd closed up 80 yen at 2,770 yen.
Toyota Motor Corp rose 50 yen to 2,780 yen.
Sony Corp closed up 90 yen at 6,860 yen.
Traders said some investors bought steelmakers' shares on hopes that the sector would benefit from a redirection of funds from the bond market.
Kawasaki Steel Corp finished up six yen at 347 yen. It was the sixth most heavily traded issue with a turnover of 3.628 million shares.
The second-section index finished up 10.55 points at 2,036.83, with 15.59 million shares traded.
The over-the-counter (OTC) index was up 0.14 point at 1,478.43.
